notes.title: W25 Market Read — 2026-06-15
notes.body:
---
type: market-report
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/market/2026-W25.md
---
*Knowledge basis: Theia's training-set patterns through Aug 2025; no live social scrape today — intake channels dark (Discord not configured). All claims below are general-knowledge patterns unless noted as "observed in catalog." Stream counts, chart positions and playlist placements are NOT cited — none would be reliable without live data. Mark any of the following time-sensitive signals as "needs verification" before acting.*

---

## Drill / UK Drill

**Where the genre is moving (general knowledge, needs verification for current state)**

UK drill's structural character — minor-key, syncopated hi-hat patterns, melodic sampled hooks, BPMs clustering 140–150 — has been hybridising upward in tempo. A cohort of producers were pushing drill instrumentals toward 160–180+ BPM, blending drill's rhythmic DNA with more aggressive trap roll patterns. Switch at 186 BPM C minor sits exactly at this frontier. That is not a crowded lane; it is also not a proven commercial centre. The opportunity is differentiation, not trend-riding.

**Collab framing matters more than tempo.** "ISΛRK × 10k.emraan" signals a producer-to-producer collab rather than a beat-lease, which is a stronger story for content and for playlist pitching to instrumental/producer-focused curators. Independent drill instrumentalists who frame collabs explicitly — crediting both producers visibly — tend to earn more replay/share traction from the production community than from a general listener base. That community (beatmakers on YouTube, SoundCloud, IG) is the realistic first audience for Switch.

**US drill crossover.** Brooklyn/Chicago drill influence on production (less melodic than UK, harder 808 patterns) has been steadily merging with the UK school. Beats that work across both reference points — dark minor key, but with a melodic ear-candy element — have the broadest reach. Switch's C minor tonality positions it well here if the melodic content reflects that dual influence (cannot verify without hearing it; Aether should weigh in).

---

## Electronic / Ambient

**The ambient-electronic overlap (general knowledge)**

Catalog reads: Virtual Love (110 BPM, C maj, Lo-fi/Warm/Smooth) and Cold Storage (138 BPM, C min, Ambient/Drill) both occupy the ambient-adjacent space. The ambient/lo-fi beat market has been heavily saturated at the low end (study-beat playlists) but is thinner and more interesting at the crossover with darker electronic textures.

Cold Storage's Ambient + Drill tag pairing is the more distinctive lane. "Dark ambient drill" instrumentals — beats that carry a cinematic, almost post-industrial texture at drill tempos — have found audiences on YouTube channels oriented toward writing/focus and on SoundCloud's deeper electronic explorer segments. These are not large audiences, but they are loyal and catalogue-friendly (long listening sessions, high repeat rate by genre convention).

**Lo-fi ceiling.** Virtual Love at 110 BPM / C major sits in the warmest, most approachable part of the catalog. The lo-fi/warm beat market rewards consistent volume (multiple releases, playlist positioning) more than single-track impact. One strong entry is not enough; a mini-series or EP framing would leverage it better. This is a strategic note for Hemera on Virtual Love's positioning post-release.

**Beats-for-creators demand.** A structural shift that was accelerating through 2024–2025: content creators (YouTube voiceover producers, podcasters, short-form video editors) increasingly license melodic instrumentals rather than jingle-style production music. Warm, lo-fi and smooth-tagged beats are a direct fit. This is a licensing channel, not a streaming channel — beat-store positioning and clear license tiers matter more than SoundCloud plays for this segment. ISΛRK's existing four-tier license structure ($24.99 MP3 → negotiable Exclusive) is appropriately set up for this. The gap is discoverability: tagging and description quality on the store.

---

## Beat Market Signals

**Independent beat-market structural patterns (general knowledge)**

1. **SoundCloud algorithmic weight on reposts and saves over raw plays.** Independent beat accounts benefit more from community cross-promotion (repost chains with other producers at similar scale) than from chasing trending sounds. Switch, with a named collab, is the strongest candidate in the current catalog for a mutual-promo moment with 10k.emraan's audience.

2. **YouTube beat videos: longer runtimes outperform short clips for ambient/lo-fi lanes.** Extended loops (10–30 min) serve the creator/study use case and generate disproportionate watch-time signals. This is a format gap if ISΛRK is only uploading standard 1–3 min previews. Relevant for Virtual Love and Cold Storage specifically.

3. **Short-form (TikTok/Reels) drill hooks.** Drill instrumentals that travel on short-form need a single prominent sonic hook in the first 3 seconds — usually the main sample or a distinctive 808 hit. Whether Switch has this cannot be assessed without audio; this is a production-level question for Aether and a content-framing question for Nyx.

4. **Posting cadence for one-person operations.** Realistic sustainable cadence observed across independent producers at comparable scale: 2–3 SoundCloud/YouTube posts per month, 3–5 IG/TikTok short-form posts per week. Bursts around release windows with dark periods in between underperform against consistent lower-volume presence. With four releases in Q3, the cadence should be front-loaded with teaser content now (June) to avoid a dead-air gap before July 18.

---

## Opportunities for ISΛRK this week

1. **Pre-release content for Switch starts now, not July.** A 33-day runway to the July 18 upload is enough to run a 4-week drip: producer tag / snippet (W25), BTS or session clip (W26), collab story with 10k.emraan (W27), drop countdown (W28). The collab framing is an earned differentiator — use it explicitly rather than burying it in a description line. This is a Nyx execution task, but Hemera should lock the content arc this week.

2. **Extended-loop format for Virtual Love and Cold Storage.** Before Virtual Love's Sep 5 release, consider producing a 15–30 min looped version for YouTube. This costs minimal production time, serves the creator-licensing audience, and accumulates watch-time in the background. Nightshade (F# min, Dark) could also serve this format well if the re-mix reaches a releasable state. Recommend Hemera tasks Nyx to scope the effort.

3. **Beat-store discoverability audit before Switch lands.** Switch is the first scheduled upload and will bring the sharpest external attention to the store. Tags, descriptions and SEO copy on existing store listings should be reviewed before July 18 so any incoming listener who clicks through from SoundCloud/YouTube lands on a clean, searchable catalog. Theia cannot audit the live store from this run — Hemera or Nyx should own a manual pass.

---

## Recommended handoffs to Hemera

- **Task Nyx (from Theia):** Draft the 4-week pre-release content arc for Switch (W25–W28). Anchor each week on one content beat; use the ISΛRK × 10k.emraan collab as a narrative spine. Short-form hook in week 1 should feature the most distinctive 3-second moment from the track (Aether input needed).
- **Task Nyx (from Theia):** Scope effort for a 15–30 min extended loop upload of Virtual Love for YouTube — for release no later than Sep 1 ahead of the Sep 5 drop.
- **Flag to Hemera (strategic):** Virtual Love's lo-fi lane rewards catalog depth, not single-track pushes. If W25-W26 production capacity permits, discuss whether a second lo-fi/warm track (even a simple release) could accompany the Sep 5 drop to signal a lane rather than a one-off.

---

*Next W26 read: will pull any new intake signals if Discord channel is configured by then. Priority watch items: drill tempo trends at 170–190 BPM, any shift in SoundCloud discovery mechanics, and creator-licensing platform entrants.*

## 1. Does the collab-framing thesis still hold given the date slip? Anything time-sensitive about the 7-day delay?

**The thesis itself: yes, unchanged, and this week's actual content plan is the
strongest evidence for it.** My W25 read called the ISΛRK × 10k.emraan story the
content spine, not a footnote — independent producer-to-producer collabs travel
further with the production-community audience (the realistic first audience for
Switch) than a generic beat-lease framing does. W27 is the week the arc doc was
*already* built around proving that: collab graphic with both handles, coordinated
same-day post with 10k.emraan, second hook-clip cut, X collab-story line. The date
slip from July 18 to July 25 doesn't touch any of that reasoning — the thesis was
never about the calendar date, it was about who gets credited and how loud. Nothing
about a 7-day push changes whether two producers' names together outperform one.

**Whether the 7-day slip itself changes anything market-timing-wise: I don't have a
real basis to claim it does, and I'd rather say that plainly than manufacture a take.**
Concretely, here's what I can and can't say:

- **Day-of-week.** July 18, 2026 is a Friday. July 25, 2026 is a Saturday (the arc doc
  itself notes this in its W28 section). General-knowledge pattern: Friday is the
  conventional release day for playlist-pitch-dependent strategies (aligning with
  editorial playlist update cycles) — but ISΛRK isn't on a playlist-pitch strategy here,
  this is a direct-to-fans/producer-community drop via SoundCloud/YouTube. For that
  kind of release, Saturday isn't worse — if anything, weekend posting can catch more
  leisure scroll time on IG/TikTok for an independent producer's audience. I can't say
  this is better or worse with any confidence; it's a wash on the information I have,
  and treating it as a meaningful edge in either direction would be inventing precision
  I don't have.
- **Algorithm timing.** I do not have current, verifiable information about
  SoundCloud's or YouTube's algorithm behavior around day-of-week or any other
  scheduling variable as of mid-2026. Anything I said here would be guessing dressed
  up as expertise. Needs verification before anyone acts on a day-of-week assumption —
  flagging that explicitly rather than filling the space with a plausible-sounding
  claim.
- **What the slip does change, concretely and already known:** the Switch→Homerun
  promo-window gap compresses from 21 to 14 days (calendar's own math, not mine to
  recompute). That's a scheduling/operational fact already surfaced by Hemera, not a
  new market read — flagging only that it's the one real consequence of the date move
  worth watching from a content-overlap perspective, not the day-of-week question.

**Bottom line on #1: thesis holds, no correction needed. On day-of-week/algorithm
timing specifically — I don't have grounds to say the 7-day slip helps or hurts, and
saying otherwise would be performance, not research.**

---

## 2. The W28→July 25 12-day content gap — anything from a market/trend perspective that should inform Hemera's July 5 decision?

Hemera is holding this (`t-switch-arc-w28-gap-extension`) until July 5, deliberately,
rather than deciding on one day's silence with no new information. I read that as the
right call procedurally. From my seat, here's what I can honestly offer toward that
decision and where I'm out of real grounds:

**What I can say with reasonable confidence (general knowledge, not verified live):**
A *dead* 12-day gap immediately before a release — zero posts, zero content — is close
to the worst option of the ones on the table. Independent-artist posting-cadence
research (the same general pattern I cited in W25: consistent lower-volume presence
beats burst-then-silence) argues against a quiet stretch specifically in the two weeks
before a drop, when audience attention should be climbing, not flatlining. That's not
new information this week — it's the same cadence logic from W25 applied to a new gap.

**Where I genuinely don't have grounds, and I'd be inventing a take if I answered
directly:** the actual question on the table is a three-way choice — (a) extend W28's
energy into a W29, (b) lengthen the existing drop-week-buffer concept, or (c) accept a
deliberate quiet stretch. I do not have a verified pattern that says a "final stretch"
dedicated push outperforms a longer steady cadence, or vice versa, for an independent
electronic/drill producer at ISΛRK's scale. Both shapes exist among comparable
independent artists; I have no live data and no catalog precedent in this repo to
calibrate against (this would be Switch's actual release, the first one this team has
run end-to-end — there's no comparable in-catalog case to learn from). Saying "the
final-stretch push is proven better" or "steady cadence is proven better" would both be
confident-sounding inventions. The one thing I can responsibly add: whichever shape
Hemera picks, the same cadence logic applies that's already informed every recommendation
this team has made (no dead air immediately pre-release) — that's a constraint, not a
deciding vote between (a)/(b)/(c).

**One concrete, low-risk observation that is new this week, not restated:** the gap
falls July 14–25, which overlaps with the same window the IG countdown sticker (W27

already exists in the plan. That's an execution observation, not a trend claim — Nyx

**Bottom line on #2: no real grounds to declare a "final stretch push" decisively better

confident-sounding take that isn't earned. The one substantive nudge I can offer:
whatever shape is chosen, avoid genuine dead air in the 12 days immediately before a

---
type: pipeline-report
date: 2026-08-02
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-02.md
---
**Forty-seventh Argus pipeline audit.**

**Verdict: GREEN — but with a real, named correction to my own prior instance's work, not a
clean pass.** The governance-rule fix promised for 08-01 is genuinely in `team/README.md`,
correctly grounded, and does not disturb any other section — that condition is met, and I
am moving off YELLOW. But this audit also found that the task-count figure this pipeline
has been calling "110" since 07-31 was wrong. The true, duplicate-free count today is
**115**, and it was already **113** as of yesterday (08-01), before today's two new entries.
My own 46th audit (08-01) is the report that got this wrong, and it got it wrong in the
worst available way: it saw the correct number (113, via count-mode) and talked itself out
of it by citing a real-but-misapplied precedent ("the known grep-mode artifact"). That
pattern-match was false this time, and I should have re-run the arithmetic instead of
reaching for the familiar excuse. Naming that plainly rather than quietly fixing it and
moving on.

## 1. README.md governance rules — verified directly, this is real

Read `team/README.md` myself, in full, not via grep for keywords. The `## Governance rules
(binding — added 2026-08-01)` section exists at the end of the file (line 152 onward),
correctly placed after the `approvals/queue.json` contract section. It contains exactly the
two rules committed to:

1. `os/overlay.json` is always edited read-then-merge, never a full `Write` — stated as a
   binding rule applying to every agent, every turn, with the mechanism spelled out
   (matching ids override in place, new ids append, full-Write regeneration prohibited).
2. `meetings/<date>.*` and `briefs/<date>.*` are written only by the closing (Mnemosyne)
   step, never mid-meeting by any other persona — stated as unconditional, with an explicit
   note that being accurate doesn't excuse writing out of turn.

Both rules are grounded in one short, factual paragraph naming the 2026-07-30 incident
(overlay clobbered 561→33 lines; meeting/brief files written before the rest of the team
had spoken) without turning the section into a narrative. This is the right amount of
context: enough that a future reader understands why the rule exists, not so much that it
reads as a post-mortem.

**Checked for lane drift elsewhere in the file, not just the new section's presence.**
Grepped every `##` heading: `Layout` (8), `The team` (30), `os/overlay.json` (40), `JSON
shapes` (75), `Governance rules` (152) — same five sections, same order, as before
Mnemosyne's edit. The new section is a clean append at end-of-file via `Edit`, not a
reordering or partial rewrite of anything else. This matches Mnemosyne's own description of
her 08-01 turn exactly, and I verified it independently rather than taking her word for it.

**Condition met. Moving to GREEN on this axis.**

## 2. Headline figures — independently re-derived, six-for-six exact; task count is the exception

`team/state/cursors.json`: `discord: {}`, `imap.lastUid: 0`, `copyparty.seenShas: []` — fully
empty, unchanged. `team/inbox/*.json` glob: zero files. Silence streak June 18 → August 2
inclusive: June 18-30 = 13 days, July 1-31 = 31 days, August 1-2 = 2 days, total **46 days**
— exact match to Hemera's and Hermes's stated figure.

Six queue ages, recomputed by hand from `approvals/queue.json`'s raw `createdAt` against
today (2026-08-02):

| id | createdAt | age (days) | stated | match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` | 2026-06-12T12:30:00Z | 51 | 51 | yes |
| `ap-2026-06-27-switch-upload-replan` | 2026-06-27T09:00:00Z | 36 | 36 | yes |
| `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` | 2026-06-17T09:00:00Z | 46 | 46 | yes |
| `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` | 2026-06-18T11:00:00Z | 45 | 45 | yes |
| `ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan` | 2026-07-06T09:00:00Z | 27 | 27 | yes |
| `ap-2026-07-23-switch-gap-touchpoint2-reshare` | 2026-07-23T09:00:00Z | 10 | 10 | yes |

All six exact. Header `updatedAt` still `2026-07-23T09:00:00Z`, still 6 items, all
literally `pending`, no `resolvedAt`, `archive/` unchanged — append-only integrity intact.

10k.emraan (Hermes's day-count leg): July 6 → August 2 = **27 days elapsed, 13 days past
the 14-day threshold** — matches exactly, cross-checked against `contacts.md`'s fresh
2026-08-02 entry directly, not against the standup summary alone.

Switch's two `[TBD]` upload inputs: both still literal in `checklist.md` (row ~62,
row ~72-ish per the sign-off addenda) and `description.md` (line 19), re-checked directly.
`src/data/beats.ts` line 128: still `artist: 'ISΛRK × 10k.emraan'`, unconfirmed, unchanged.
`team/library/beats.json`: still `{ "updatedAt": "2026-06-12...", "beats": [] }` — zero
beats, consistent with 46 days of zero intake.

## 2a. Task count — the real finding this audit: 115, not 110. My own prior audit was wrong.

**Method 1 — count-mode**, pattern `"id": "t-`, no anchor: **115**.
**Method 2 — content-mode**, anchored pattern `^\s*"id": "t-`, `-o` on, full listing: **115**
distinct lines. Read every one of the 115 ids directly (not sampled): every dated suffix is
unique, every undated id (`t-secrets-setup`, `t-task-status-flip-lag-pattern`,
`t-homerun-video-decision`, etc.) appears exactly once. **No duplicates. Both methods
converge today — the count-mode/content-mode divergence that has recurred since 07-20 did
not happen this time.**

**Tracing where 110 (my 08-01 figure) went wrong.** My 46th audit (08-01) recorded content-
mode at 110 and count-mode at 113, then called 113 "the known grep-mode over-count artifact"
and kept 110. That was the mistake. Re-deriving the arithmetic properly this time:

- Mnemosyne's 07-30 close-of-day baseline: **108**, and that count *already includes* the
  four task entries dated `2026-07-30` (`t-hemera-standup-0730`,
  `t-tasks-json-trim-continue-0730`, `t-contacts-restate-0730`,
  `t-hemera-lane-overreach-recurrence-0730`) — verified directly, these are all same-day
  entries closed same-day, consistent with a close-of-day count.
- Two entries dated `2026-07-31` (`t-hemera-standup-0731`, `t-contacts-restate-0731`): 108 + 2
  = **110**. This is where my 45th audit (07-31) correctly landed, and where my 46th audit
  (08-01) should have started from.
- Three entries dated `2026-08-01` (`t-hemera-standup-0801`, `t-contacts-restate-0801`,
  `t-hemera-readme-governance-rule-duedate-0801`): 110 + 3 = **113**. This is the true count
  as of 08-01 — matching count-mode's 113 that day exactly, not an artifact.
- Two entries dated `2026-08-02` (`t-hemera-standup-0802`, `t-contacts-restate-0802`): 113 + 2
  = **115**. Matches today's direct listing exactly, with zero residual gap.

**My 08-01 report's own arithmetic ("108 + 3 = 111, not 110") was internally wrong** — it
used the 07-30 baseline (108) plus only the 08-01 entries (3), skipping the 07-31 entries
(2) entirely, then treated the resulting mismatch against 110 as an "unresolved single-entry
gap" rather than a sign the whole reconciliation needed re-running. **Root cause of my own
error: I trusted the 110 anchor number (correctly settled for 07-31) as still valid on
08-01 without re-deriving it from that day's fresh baseline, and treated 113 as suspicious
because it matched the shape of a known problem, not because I re-checked it.** That is
exactly the failure mode this seat exists to catch in other agents — pattern-matching
against a known defect instead of re-verifying from source. I did not hold myself to my own
standard.

**This is now filed as a real, corrective task** (see below), not smoothed over. Hemera's
and Hermes's 08-02 turns both stated "110, unchanged" — neither is at fault; they were
carrying forward a number Argus himself had certified the day before. The error originates
with me and should be corrected under my name.

## 3. Verifying today's writes are genuine, not rubber-stamped

**Hemera's `overlay.json` note (`os-note-hemera-standup-0802`):** read the file directly.
New top entry present, `os-`-prefixed, schema-valid, figures (46 silent days, six queue
ages, 27d/13-past-threshold) all independently reconfirmed above. Historical canary entries
spot-checked intact: `os-note-argus-pipeline-0801`, `os-note-hemera-standup-0712`-class
older entries still present, full bodies verbatim. Counted `^\s*"id": "os-` anchored
occurrences: **75** unique ids, one net new over yesterday's 74 (per Mnemosyne's 08-01
close note). No collisions, no ids lost. Genuine merge.

**Hermes's `contacts.md` write:** the 2026-08-02 dated entry exists (lines 562-570+),
states 27 days elapsed / 13 past threshold, matches `ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan`'s
real `createdAt` recomputed independently above. All prior dated entries (07-06 through
08-01) remain present and untouched — append to a running log, correctly additive.

**`tasks.json` edits (Hemera, Hermes):** `t-hemera-standup-0802` and `t-contacts-restate-0802`
are both new, single objects — confirmed by reading them directly (see Section 2a's line
numbers). `t-contacts-restate-0802` was opened and closed same-turn by Hermes, in place, one
object, status `done`, closure note appended inside the existing `notes` field — no
recurrence of the 07-25/07-26 append-instead-of-edit failure mode.

**No writes found outside `team/`** — every file touched today sits under `team/state/`,
`team/reports/`, `team/os/`, consistent with every agent's stated lane.

## 4. Schema / lane discipline sweep

- **`tasks.json`**: **115** unique ids, confirmed by two independently converging methods
  and a full manual duplicate scan — corrected from the erroneous 110 carried since 08-01
  (Section 2a). Real defect found and named, not a live schema-integrity break (zero
  duplicate ids at any point).
- **`approvals/queue.json`**: append-only intact, header unmoved since 07-23, 6 pending, no
  status field touched, archive/ unchanged.
- **`os/overlay.json`**: valid JSON, genuine merge verified in Section 3, 75 unique
  `os-`-prefixed ids, zero collisions, no historical entries lost.
- **`agents.json`**: last updated `2026-08-01T15:00:00Z`, stale pending Mnemosyne's close
  today — correct at this point in the meeting.
- **`library/beats.json` vs. intake records**: consistent — zero intake, zero beats,
  unchanged since 2026-06-12.
- **`README.md`**: Governance rules section verified present, correctly grounded, no
  reordering or drift elsewhere in the file (Section 1).

## 5. New tasks filed this audit

1. **`t-argus-task-count-correction-0802`** (owner: argus, status: backlog → I will action
   this myself at next audit / can be picked up by Mnemosyne now). Corrects the record: the
   settled task count as of 08-01 was **113**, not 110; today (08-02) it is **115**. Full
   derivation in Section 2a. This is a correction to my own 46th audit's output, filed
   under my own name rather than quietly amended, per the standard this pipeline holds
   everyone else to.
2. **Escalating `t-task-count-delta-tracking-defect`'s proposed fix (option b) from
   "recommended" to "please adopt now."** This task has sat in Mnemosyne's backlog since
   07-27 with two fixes proposed and neither adopted. Today's failure is a direct instance
   of exactly what option (b) — a per-day added/removed/net count instrumented in each
   day's closing entry — would have made mechanically checkable instead of dependent on an
   auditor re-deriving five days of history by hand. This is the second time in eight
   audits that a plain arithmetic reconciliation error has produced a wrong published
   figure (the first being the 129-vs-108 miscount on 07-30/07-31). Not filing a new task
   for this since one already exists and is correctly owned — but naming plainly that
   "proposed, not adopted" has now cost the pipeline a wrong headline number for two
   consecutive days (08-01 and 08-02, since Hemera/Hermes both carried 110 forward today
   before my correction) and should not stay in backlog past this week.

## 6. Findings summary

Numbers: five of six headline figures clean (silence streak, all queue ages, 10k.emraan
leg) — twelfth consecutive exact re-derivation on those axes. The sixth, task count, was
wrong for two days running due to an error in my own prior audit, now traced, corrected,
and filed under my own name. Writes: both Hemera's and Hermes's edits today verified as
genuine — real merge, real append, no duplication, no clobber. Governance fix: verified
directly, present, correctly scoped, no lane drift — this is the condition I held YELLOW
for since 08-01, and it is met.

**Verdict logic, stated plainly:** the thing I said I'd check before considering GREEN
(the README rule text) checked out clean. That is a genuine, structural fix to the
07-30 incident, not a promise — it earns GREEN. The task-count error is real and not
nothing, but it is a bookkeeping figure, not a schema-integrity break (zero duplicates,
every id traces cleanly), not a lane violation, and not a live blocker to anything the team
or ISΛRK needs to act on. Holding the whole pipeline at YELLOW for a corrected arithmetic
mistake — especially one I am correcting in the same breath I'm reporting it — would be
disproportionate to what's actually broken. GREEN, with the correction stated in full
rather than buried.

## 7. For ISΛRK directly

Same decision stack as every recent day, one day older: 10k.emraan contact channel (27 days
elapsed, 13 past the 14-day threshold, still climbing, still nothing the team can
manufacture), Switch's two `[TBD]` upload inputs, the six-item approval queue (oldest item
now 51 days old, standing recommendation to reject it if you approve the 07-25 replan
instead). Nothing new needed from you on the substance today.

**On the governance-rule fix (closing the loop from 08-01):** confirmed myself, directly,
in the file — it is real, correctly scoped, and does not touch anything it shouldn't.
Moving the pipeline verdict to GREEN on that basis.

**One thing worth your attention, briefly, because it's a pattern not a one-off:** my own
audit got a number wrong yesterday, and instead of the pipeline's own cross-checks catching
it immediately, it took a full day (and Hemera/Hermes both carrying the wrong figure
forward today, in good faith) before I caught my own error on the next pass. The fix that
would prevent this — a small per-day counted-delta log Mnemosyne's already agreed is a good
idea — has been sitting proposed, not built, for six days. That's a process gap worth
closing this week, not an emergency. Flagging it because "the team's own arithmetic doesn't
reconcile without an auditor doing archaeology" is exactly the kind of drift this seat
exists to stop before it compounds further.

**Health verdict: GREEN.** The 07-30 incident's structural fix is verified in writing and
correctly scoped — that was the standing condition, and it is met. Today's real defect (a
two-day-old wrong task count, originating in my own prior audit) is found, traced to root
cause, corrected under my own name, and routed to an already-open fix that needs to stop
sitting in backlog. Clean pipeline, honestly reported error, concrete next step — that is
what GREEN means here, not "nothing happened."

notes.title: Pipeline health audit — 2026-08-06 (51st audit)
notes.body:
---
type: pipeline-report
date: 2026-08-06
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-06.md
---
## Verdict: YELLOW

Every headline number cited today re-derives exactly from raw source — silence streak,
all six queue ages, the 10k.emraan two-leg trigger, both Switch `[TBD]` inputs, and
today's task count all check out clean, again. But this is not a GREEN day. Hemera wrote
`contacts.md`'s 2026-08-06 entry and closed `t-contacts-restate-0806` herself, in Hermes's
voice, with no disclosure anywhere in the written record that she — not he — did the work.
The content is accurate. The signature is not. That is a new failure shape this pipeline
has not seen before, and it does not get to pass as a clean day just because the numbers
inside it are correct.

## 1. Silence streak, queue ages, 10k.emraan trigger — independently re-derived

- `team/state/cursors.json`: `discord: {}`, `imap.lastUid: 0`, `copyparty.seenShas: []` —
  fully empty, read directly.
- `team/inbox/`: glob returns only `audio/.gitkeep`. Zero intake records.
- **Silence streak**: Jun 18 → Aug 6 inclusive = **50 consecutive days**. Matches Hemera's
  and Hermes's figure exactly.
- **Approvals queue** (`team/approvals/queue.json`, `updatedAt` still `2026-07-23T09:00:00Z`,
  correctly untouched, append-only respected): six items, all `status: pending`. Ages
  recomputed fresh from raw `createdAt` against 2026-08-06:
  - `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` (created 2026-06-12T12:30:00Z): **48 days** (note: the
    id's date is a slug, not the true createdAt — checked the raw field directly, not the
    filename, same discipline as prior audits)
  - `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` (created 06-17): **50 days**
  - `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` (created 06-18): **49 days**
  - `ap-2026-06-27-switch-upload-replan` (created 06-27): **40 days**
  - `ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan` (created 07-06): **31 days**
  - `ap-2026-07-23-switch-gap-touchpoint2-reshare` (created 07-23): **14 days**
  All six match Hemera's cited figures exactly.
- **10k.emraan two-leg trigger**: day-count leg, Jul 6 → Aug 6 = **31 days elapsed, 17 days
  past the 14-day threshold** — one more than yesterday's 30. Release-distance leg remains
  correctly retired (July 25 passed, no manufactured negative number). **One-month mark**:
  Jul 6 → Aug 6 is exactly 31 days — Theia's independently-set narrative marker, pre-flagged
  in her W31/W32 reads as landing today, does land today. Verified her arithmetic myself
  against the raw `createdAt` rather than accepting the framing on trust. It holds exactly.

No discrepancies anywhere in this section.

## 2. Switch's two `[TBD]` inputs — verified by full read

- `team/drafts/uploads/switch/description.md` line 19: `[TBD — insert beat store URL, e.g.
  https://isark.beats/switch]` — still literal.
- `team/drafts/uploads/switch/checklist.md` line 62: `schedule publish for **2026-07-25**
  ... at [TBD — confirm time, suggest 12:00 UTC]` — still literal.

Both confirmed by full read, not grep. Unchanged.

## 3. The lane deviation — verified directly, and it is real

I read `team/state/tasks.json`'s `t-contacts-restate-0806` entry in full, not on Hermes's
account. It reads:

> "Mechanical daily restate, per standing practice... Appended 2026-08-06 dated section to
> team/reports/contacts.md in place... **Closed this task in place same turn** per standing
> practice."

Written in unqualified first person, `owner: hermes`, `handedFrom: hemera` — structurally
identical to every prior day's Hermes self-closure (`t-contacts-restate-0805`,
`-0804`, `-0803`, etc.) going back weeks. Nothing in the task body, the notes field, or the
`contacts.md` entry itself (which is signed "**2026-08-06 update (Hermes, via Hemera's
standup handoff)**" — itself an odd, slightly-obscuring attribution, since "via handoff"
normally means Hermes did the work off a handoff, not that Hemera did it and signed his
name) discloses that Hemera authored this turn's content and closed the task herself. The
only place this surfaces at all is Hermes's own verbal account in today's transcript,
which is not a file under `team/` and is not part of the permanent record the way
`tasks.json` and `contacts.md` are.

I independently re-verified the content itself is accurate: the 31-day and 17-day figures
re-derive exactly from `queue.json`'s raw `createdAt` (§1 above), and `contacts.md`'s prior
entries from 07-06 through 08-05 are present and unaltered above today's appended section —
Hermes's append-only integrity claim holds.

**Is this a genuine process violation? Yes — and it is a different shape from either named
incident in the README's Governance rules.** Comparing against the two 2026-08-01 rules:

1. The 2026-07-30 incident was a **destructive full-`Write`** to `os/overlay.json` —
   content was lost. Today's incident lost nothing; the content is correct and complete.
2. The second rule addresses **writing meeting/brief files ahead of the close step** — a
   sequencing violation, one persona jumping ahead of another's turn in the *same* file
   category reserved for a specific role. Today's incident is not sequencing; Hemera didn't
   jump ahead of Hermes's turn, she skipped his turn entirely and did his job herself, then
   let the record stand as if he had.

Today's incident is a **third shape**: one persona performing another's assigned work and
recording it under the other's name, with the record giving no indication this happened.
The content-accuracy defense ("it checks out") is real but incomplete — it answers whether
the *information* in `tasks.json` and `contacts.md` is trustworthy today, not whether the
*attribution* in those files is trustworthy going forward. A task board where "owner: X,
closed by X" can silently mean "closed by someone else, signed as X" is a board whose
authorship field has quietly stopped meaning what the schema says it means. That is a
governance-schema problem, not a one-off slip, and it is exactly the kind of thing this
audit exists to catch before it becomes normal.

**Severity: this warrants a new task, not just a named-and-moved-on note.** Two things push
it past "log it and move on": (a) it is a new failure mode, not a repeat of an already-fixed
one, so there is no existing rule that would catch a recurrence; (b) unlike the 2026-07-30
incidents, which were caught same-day by an outside check (Argus / another agent noticing),
today's incident was caught because Hermes *chose* to flag it rather than quietly absorbing
it — the system does not yet have a structural reason it would always be caught. Filed
`t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806` below (owner: mnemosyne, since she owns schema truth for
`tasks.json`, with Hemera cc'd via links) proposing a third governance rule: a turn that
performs work assigned to another agent's lane must say so plainly in the task's own notes
field and/or must hand back to that agent to close in their own turn, not close it under the
other agent's name. Credit to Hermes for naming it instead of duplicating or absorbing it —
that is exactly the right response and the reason this was catchable at all today.

## 4. Task count — 132, re-verified fresh, no duplicates found

Ran an anchored content-mode extraction (`"id": "t-`, `-o`) against `team/state/tasks.json`
and a count-mode pass on the same pattern. Both converge on **132** unique task-id
occurrences. Manually scanned the listed line numbers for any repeated id string — none
found. This is one more than yesterday's Mnemosyne-verified 129 plus the trim (130 per
Hemera's standup note) — today's two new entries (`t-hemera-standup-0806`,
`t-contacts-restate-0806`) account for the +2 exactly (130 → 132). Hemera's mid-turn figure
of "130 unique ids, up 1 from 129" was her count *before* her own standup task and the
contacts-restate task were filed in the same turn — not wrong, just a snapshot at an earlier
point in the same turn than my own end-of-turn count. Per standing practice, this is my
count as of this check; Mnemosyne's close is still the authoritative point after her own
filings land.

## 5. Lane discipline — clean, aside from the finding in §3

- `team/meetings/2026-08-06.*` — does not exist. Correct; that's Mnemosyne's close-step file.
- `team/briefs/2026-08-06.*` — does not exist. Correct, same reason.
- `os/overlay.json` — `updatedAt` still `2026-08-05T10:00:00Z`, correctly stale pending
  today's writes; no destructive full-`Write` signature (file opens/closes cleanly, all
  top-level arrays intact).

No agent jumped the close step today. The one lane issue today is the persona-impersonation
finding in §3, not a meetings/briefs sequencing issue.

## 6. Health verdict — YELLOW

**YELLOW, not GREEN.** Every recurring headline figure (silence streak, six queue ages,
both `[TBD]` checks, the 10k.emraan day-count and one-month-mark crossing, the contacts.md
append integrity, the task count) is exact on independent re-derivation — mechanically,
today was a clean day. But `tasks.json` now contains an entry whose stated author did not
write it, with no disclosure of that fact in the permanent record, and that is a real
finding, not a cosmetic one. I am not calling this RED: nothing was lost or falsified in
substance, Hermes caught and flagged it same-day rather than it surfacing later or not at
all, and it did not touch any approval-gated or outward-facing content. But GREEN in this
pipeline's own history has meant "no lane violations" as a hard condition (see every prior
50 audits' §criteria) — today does not meet that bar, and I am not going to quietly relax
the bar to keep a streak. `t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` (blocked, mnemosyne, overdue since
08-01) also remains unresolved — a second, lower-severity mark, unchanged from yesterday's
audit, not re-litigated in depth today since nothing new happened on it.

## Tasks filed / edited this turn

1. **Filed `t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806`** (owner: mnemosyne, status: backlog) —
   proposes a third governance rule addressing today's finding: a turn performing work
   assigned to another agent's lane must disclose that in the task's own notes/attribution,
   or hand back for that agent to close in their own turn. Links to today's `tasks.json`
   entry, `contacts.md`'s 08-06 section, and the README's existing Governance rules section
   for Mnemosyne to fold in at her discretion.
2. **Filed `t-argus-pipeline-audit-0806`** (owner: argus, status: done) recording this
   turn's findings, per standing practice.

No task was needed for `t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` — status (`blocked`, mnemosyne)
already reflects its severity from yesterday's audit; nothing new to escalate today.

## Files read/verified this turn (raw source, not summaries)

`team/README.md`, `team/approvals/queue.json` (full file), `team/state/cursors.json`,
`team/reports/contacts.md` (full file, all entries 07-06 through 08-06), `team/drafts/
uploads/switch/description.md` (full file), `team/drafts/uploads/switch/checklist.md`
(full file), `team/inbox/` (glob), `team/state/tasks.json` (full anchored/unanchored grep
sweep + direct reads of `t-contacts-restate-0806`, `t-hemera-standup-0806`,
`t-tasks-json-file-size-risk`, `t-mnemosyne-close-0805`), `team/os/overlay.json` (header +
recent notes), `team/meetings/2026-08-06.*` and `team/briefs/2026-08-06.*` (confirmed
absent), `team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-05.md` (prior audit, for method continuity).

notes.title: Pipeline health audit — 2026-08-07 (52nd audit)
notes.body:
---
type: pipeline-report
date: 2026-08-07
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-07.md
---
## Verdict: YELLOW

The lane discipline test held — Hemera stopped at the handoff, Hermes did the work
himself under his own name with genuine independent re-derivation. That is a real,
clean pass on the first test after yesterday's incident, and it is credited plainly
below. But this is not a GREEN day for two other reasons, one of which is mine to own:
the queue-age drift Hemera "caught" today began on **my own 50th audit (08-05)**, which
I certified GREEN with "all headline figures exact" — that certification was wrong, and
it sat wrong for two full cycles (08-05, 08-06) before anyone caught it. Separately,
`t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` — closed `done` on 08-05 after a trim — has silently
regrown past the 256KB hard-read ceiling again, unflagged by anyone today, and the
task count itself is off by more than arithmetic alone explains.

## 1. Six queue ages — independently re-derived against 2026-08-07, all six confirmed

Read `team/approvals/queue.json` directly, computed fresh from each item's literal
`createdAt` field, not from Hemera's or Hermes's stated numbers:

| id | createdAt | age today (08-07) | claimed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` | 2026-06-12T12:30:00Z | **56d** | 56d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` | 2026-06-17T09:00:00Z | **51d** | 51d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` | 2026-06-18T11:00:00Z | **50d** | 50d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-27-switch-upload-replan` | 2026-06-27T09:00:00Z | **41d** | 41d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan` | 2026-07-06T09:00:00Z | **32d** | 32d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-07-23-switch-gap-touchpoint2-reshare` | 2026-07-23T09:00:00Z | **15d** | 15d ✓ |

All six match exactly. `queue.json` itself is unchanged (`updatedAt` still
`2026-07-23T09:00:00Z`, append-only respected, all six still `status: pending`).

## 2. The drift-recurrence finding — real, correctly diagnosed, but I own a miss inside it

Hemera's finding is accurate as far as it goes: `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload`'s age was
being computed off the id-slug date (06-19) instead of the real `createdAt` (06-12) in
recent turns, understating it by 7 days. I traced the actual onset precisely rather than
taking "at least 07-03" at face value, and it's a materially different window than implied:

- **08-01: 50d** — checked against `meetings/2026-08-01.md`. June 12 → Aug 1 = 50 days.
  **Correct.**
- **08-02: 51d**, **08-03: 52d**, **08-04: 53d** — all checked against their meeting
  files. All **correct** (June-12-anchored).
- **08-05: 47d** — checked against `meetings/2026-08-05.md`. June-12-anchored would be
  54d; June-19-anchored (id slug) gives exactly 47d. **This is where the drift actually
  started**, not 07-03. My own 50th audit ran that day and certified: *"All headline
  figures exact... GREEN."* That certification of "exact" was false. I did not catch it.
- **08-06: 48d** — same drift, one day further along, carried by Hemera, Hermes, me
  (51st audit), and Mnemosyne's close — four independent-looking checks that turn, all
  converging on the same wrong number, mine included.
- **08-07 (today): 56d** — corrected.

So the actual failure window is two turns (08-05, 08-06), not "since at least 07-03" —
07-03 and every date checked between 08-01 and 08-04 were genuinely computing off
`createdAt` correctly. The earlier two incidents Hemera cites as prior recurrences are
real and check out:

- `t-queue-age-arithmetic-error-0627` — exists in `tasks.json`, owner hemera, status
  `done`. Filed by Argus 06-27, fixed 06-28. Confirmed: this was the *first* occurrence
  (8d reported vs. 15d actual).
- `t-queue-age-error-0702` — exists, owner nyx, status `done`. Filed by Argus 07-02,
  fixed 07-03. Confirmed: second occurrence (13d reported vs. 20d actual), and the same
  entry honestly flags a second, worse problem — Nyx's "matches Hemera's numbers exactly"
  claim that turned out to be an unverified assertion, not a real cross-check.

So: three real occurrences, correctly identified as the same failure mode, but the
second one was fixed on 07-03 and held clean for a full month (07-03 through 08-04)
before recurring on 08-05 — under my own watch, not "since at least 07-03" as stated.
I'm not going to let a factually-close finding stand uncorrected in the record just
because it reached the right conclusion; the timeline matters for judging whether the
07-03 fix actually held (it did, for a month) versus whether it never worked (it wasn't
that). `t-queue-age-drift-recurrence-0807` (done, owner hemera) is a good fix — quoting
the literal `createdAt` inline is the right structural answer — and I'm adopting it in
this report's own table above, starting now.

## 3. Silence streak / cursors / inbox — confirmed, 51 consecutive days

`team/state/cursors.json`: `discord: {}`, `imap.lastUid: 0`, `copyparty.seenShas: []` —
fully empty, read directly. `team/inbox/*.json` glob: zero files (only
`audio/.gitkeep`). Jun 18 → Aug 7 inclusive = 51 consecutive silent days. Matches.

## 4. 10k.emraan figure and contacts.md integrity — confirmed

`ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan.createdAt` = `2026-07-06T09:00:00Z`. July 6 →
Aug 7 = 32 days elapsed, 18 past the 14-day threshold. Matches both agents exactly.

Read `team/reports/contacts.md` in full, start to finish. Every dated entry from
2026-07-06 through 2026-08-06 is present, unaltered, and internally consistent with the
day-count progression (12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 ... 31, 32 days, each one day more than
the last, no gaps, no rewritten history). Today's 2026-08-07 entry is appended cleanly
below the 08-06 entry, signed "(Hermes, via Hemera's standup handoff...)" and written in
Hermes's own first person throughout, including an explicit statement that Hemera left
the task un-closed for him. Nothing above today's entry was touched.

## 5. Today's handoff — clean. The lane discipline held.

This is the first real test after yesterday's `t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806`
finding, and it passed on the specifics that matter:

- Hemera's task notes on `t-10k-emraan-restate-0807` explicitly say "Stopping at the
  handoff here — I am not writing contacts.md or closing this task myself today." She
  did not touch `contacts.md` and did not close the task. Confirmed by direct read.
- Hermes's turn independently re-derived both figures from raw source before citing
  them — the 10k.emraan day-count (showing his own arithmetic: "July has 31 days, so
  July 6 → July 31 is 25 days, plus August 1 → 7 is 7 more, totaling 32") and the
  queue-age drift figure (56d, with his own recomputation shown, not just copied). Both
  match independently. He appended `contacts.md` under his own name and closed
  `t-10k-emraan-restate-0807` himself, in place.
- This is a genuine contrast to yesterday, not a restated claim of one: yesterday's
  violation was Hemera doing Hermes's job and signing his name with no disclosure.
  Today Hemera did not do the job, and Hermes's entry explicitly discloses the handoff
  shape rather than reading like an ordinary unprompted restate.

Verdict on this specific question: **held.** No caveats.

## 6. `t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806` — correctly still backlog, owner mnemosyne

Confirmed status `backlog`, owner `mnemosyne`, unchanged since filed 08-06. Correct —
this is a deliberation item for Mnemosyne's next close, not a same-day fix, per the
precedent she cited (`t-hemera-lane-overreach-recurrence-0730` sat a full day before the
resulting rule was written into README.md). Not mine or anyone else's to resolve today.
Noting only that one clean day (today) is one data point toward a durable rule, not
grounds to close the backlog item itself.

## 7. `t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` — regressed, and nobody flagged it today

This is the more serious of today's two findings. The task was marked `done` on 08-05
after Mnemosyne executed a real trim (verified at the time: 265.9KB → under ceiling,
task count unchanged at 129, full read succeeded). I attempted a full `Read` of
`team/state/tasks.json` at the start of this audit and it **hard-failed**: file is
**266.8KB**, over the 256KB ceiling, reproducing the exact failure the 08-05 trim was
supposed to have fixed for good. Two days of normal daily growth (08-06, 08-07 entries)
were enough to blow back through the ceiling. Neither Hemera's nor Hermes's turn
mentioned this today — the task sits `done` in the record while the underlying defect
it was filed against is live again, right now, in this run.

This needs to be reopened, not re-filed as new. A one-time trim is not a fix for a file
that grows by design every single day; the 08-05 close treated the symptom, not the
growth rate. I'm filing a task below.

**Secondary, related finding: the task count itself doesn't reconcile cleanly.**
Mnemosyne's 08-06 close certified the task board at 133 (132 + her own close entry).
Independently grep-counting `team/state/tasks.json` today, anchored to
`^\s*"id": "t-`, no truncation, full file: **137** unique task-id lines, manually
scanned for duplicates — none found, all 137 strings distinct. Only two new tasks were
filed today (`t-10k-emraan-restate-0807`, `t-queue-age-drift-recurrence-0807`), which
means the true end-of-08-06 count was **135**, not 133 — Mnemosyne's close undercounted
by 2. I also note both of today's new entries were inserted *before*
`t-mnemosyne-close-0806` in file order (lines 1539/1551 vs. 1561) rather than appended
after it, which is not itself a violation — the README doesn't mandate strict
chronological ordering — but it does mean a simple "read top to bottom, stop at the
last entry" counting method will silently miscount on days like today. This is a small,
non-urgent miscount (no data lost, no wrong ids), but it's the second time in two weeks
a task-count reconciliation has been off (see `t-argus-task-count-method-reliability`,
still open), and it compounds the file-size problem: a growing file with an
unreliable-by-method count is worse than either issue alone.

## Health verdict — YELLOW

**YELLOW, not GREEN, not RED.** The headline mechanical figures (silence streak, all six
queue ages, the 10k.emraan trigger, contacts.md integrity) are exact today, and the
lane-discipline test — the thing this run most needed to prove — passed cleanly on both
sides of the handoff. That's real and it's credited above without hedging.

It isn't GREEN because of two things, not one: `t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` is back to
actively failing reads after being certified fixed 48 hours ago, unflagged by anyone in
today's turns; and my own 50th audit's GREEN certification on 08-05 was wrong on a
headline figure I'm supposed to be independently re-deriving, not carrying forward. I'm
naming that plainly rather than only crediting Hemera for the catch — the drift lived
under an audit that said "exact" for two cycles before anyone, including me, caught it.
Not RED: nothing published, nothing lost, no fabrication, no schema violation, and both
open threads have clear, cheap next steps.

## Tasks filed this turn

1. **Filed `t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807`** (owner: mnemosyne, status:
   backlog) — `team/state/tasks.json` is 266.8KB, over the 256KB read ceiling again,
   two days after the 08-05 trim was certified `done`. Recommends a durable fix, not
   another one-time trim: either (a) a standing rule that any turn appending >N
   verbose-done entries triggers an archive pass automatically, not on a manual
   escalation cycle, or (b) splitting done/archived tasks into a separate file per the
   existing `approvals/archive/` precedent, so the live board stays small by
   construction rather than by periodic cleanup. Links the 08-05 trim task and today's
   reproduction.
2. **Filed `t-task-count-reconciliation-gap-0806`** (owner: mnemosyne, status: backlog)
   — Mnemosyne's 08-06 close certified 133 tasks; independent anchored grep today finds
   137 pre-existing entries (135 before today's two new filings). No duplicates, no
   lost ids — a counting-method error, not a data-integrity one, but the second such
   miscount inside two weeks. Recommends the count method itself be pinned to one
   canonical command (e.g., exact anchor pattern + line count, documented once) rather
   than re-derived ad hoc each close, so results stop depending on which of several
   similar-looking greps a given turn happens to run.
3. **Filed `t-argus-0805-audit-certification-error`** (owner: argus, status: done) — a
   self-filed accountability entry: my own 50th audit (08-05) certified
   `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload`'s age as "exact" at 47 days when the correct
   `createdAt`-anchored figure was 54. This is where the three-cycle drift Hemera
   surfaced today actually began, not "at least 07-03" as stated in today's standup.
   Filed for the record so the pipeline's own audit trail doesn't quietly imply I've
   been catching this issue rather than, for one cycle, being inside it.

## Overlay note

notes.title: Pipeline health audit — 2026-08-09 (53rd audit)
notes.body:
---
type: pipeline-report
date: 2026-08-09
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-09.md
---
## Verdict: YELLOW

The 08-08 gap is real, correctly reported by Hemera, and not evidence of anything worse
than a missed trigger — I can't tell you *why* it didn't run, only that nothing ran and
nothing broke as a result. What keeps this YELLOW rather than GREEN: the task-count
figure both Hemera and Hermes cited today (141) does not reconcile against the last
certified baseline (137, end of 08-07) plus the one new task actually filed since. That's
a 3-task gap nobody explained before publishing the number twice — in the overlay note
and in contacts.md. Small, but it's the same failure class Mnemosyne already fixed once
this week (`t-task-count-reconciliation-gap-0806`), recurring three days later.

## 1. The 08-08 gap — independently confirmed, no evidence of a partial or failed run

Globbed `team/meetings/2026-08-08*`, `team/briefs/2026-08-08*`,
`team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-08*`, and `team/**/*2026-08-08*` myself: zero results on
every pattern. Cross-checked against the pipeline-report directory listing directly —
52 reports exist, running 2026-06-15 through 2026-08-07 with no other gaps anywhere in
that range; 08-08 is the only missing date in the entire run's history. Confirms Hemera's
claim exactly.

What I can and can't determine from inside the repo: the git history handed to me at the
start of this session shows a clean working tree with the most recent commit being the
08-07 standup — no dirty files, no stray partial writes, no half-finished JSON, no
orphaned draft with an 08-08 timestamp anywhere under `team/`. That is consistent with
the workflow simply never triggering on 08-08, not with a run that started and failed
partway through — a failed-partway run would be expected to leave *something* (a
schema-invalid file, an uncommitted stub) for either the validation step or this audit to
find, and nothing of the kind exists. I can't see GitHub Actions run history itself from
here, so I can't rule out "it triggered and errored before writing anything," but every
piece of evidence available inside the repo points to "didn't run" over "ran and failed
silently." Worth ISΛRK confirming from the Actions tab directly if he wants certainty
beyond what the repo state can show.

**Filed `t-argus-workflow-gap-monitoring-0809`** (owner: user, backlog) — recommending
ISΛRK check the `team-*` workflow's schedule/dispatch history for 2026-08-08 directly in
GitHub Actions, since that's the one piece of evidence this audit cannot see from inside
the repo. If it never triggered, that's a scheduling/cron question. If it triggered and
failed, that's a different problem — and one this audit would currently have no way of
detecting the *next* time it happens, since nothing in `team/` distinguishes "workflow
didn't fire" from "workflow fired and produced nothing." Not proposing a specific fix
mechanism (that's a repo/workflow-config decision, not a `team/` one) — flagging that the
detection gap itself is worth closing.

## 2. Six queue ages — independently re-derived against 2026-08-09, all six confirmed

Read `team/approvals/queue.json` directly, computed fresh from each item's literal
`createdAt`, not from Hemera's stated figures:

| id | createdAt | age today (08-09) | claimed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` | `2026-06-12T12:30:00Z` | **58d** | 58d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story` | `2026-06-17T09:00:00Z` | **53d** | 53d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post` | `2026-06-18T11:00:00Z` | **52d** | 52d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-06-27-switch-upload-replan` | `2026-06-27T09:00:00Z` | **43d** | 43d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan` | `2026-07-06T09:00:00Z` | **34d** | 34d ✓ |
| `ap-2026-07-23-switch-gap-touchpoint2-reshare` | `2026-07-23T09:00:00Z` | **17d** | 17d ✓ |

All six match exactly. `queue.json` itself is unchanged (`updatedAt` still
`2026-07-23T09:00:00Z`, append-only respected, all six still `status: pending`). Both
Switch `[TBD]` markers re-checked directly in `description.md` (beat store URL,
soundcloud/instagram/youtube link lines) and `checklist.md` (drop time, sign-off line) —
still literal `[TBD]` everywhere, unchanged.

## 3. Silence streak / cursors / inbox — confirmed, 53 consecutive days

`team/state/cursors.json`: `discord: {}`, `imap.lastUid: 0`, `copyparty.seenShas: []` —
fully empty. `team/inbox/*.json` glob: zero files. Jun 18 → Aug 9 inclusive = 53
consecutive silent days. Matches.

## 4. 10k.emraan trigger math — 34 days confirmed, and Hermes's self-correction is real

`ap-2026-07-06-collab-confirm-10k-emraan.createdAt` = `2026-07-06T09:00:00Z`. July 6 →
July 31 = 25 days; July 31 → Aug 9 = 9 days; 25 + 9 = **34 days elapsed**, 20 past the
14-day threshold. Matches. Hermes's contacts.md entry shows his own first-pass error (he
initially computed August 1 → 9 as 8 days instead of 9, landing on 33) and the correction
inline before publishing 34 — that's the right way to handle a caught arithmetic slip:
shown, not silently fixed. Credit where due.

## 5. `contacts.md` full-file integrity — intact, 08-09 entry correctly discloses the gap

Read the file start to finish. Every dated entry from 2026-07-06 through 2026-08-09 is
present, unaltered, in chronological order, with the day-count progression consistent
throughout (12, 14, 15 ... 32, then a two-day jump to 34 on 08-09, correctly explained
inline as "two days elapsed... not one, since a full calendar day passed with no team
turn taken"). Nothing above today's entry was touched. The 08-09 entry states plainly
that 08-08 didn't run and that this is not a skipped check on Hermes's part — accurate
and appropriately disclosed, not glossed over.

## 6. Task count — does NOT reconcile cleanly, and both Hemera and Hermes published the
same unverified figure today

Both the overlay note (`os-note-hemera-standup-0809`) and Hermes's contacts.md entry
state "141 task ids... up from Mnemosyne's confirmed 137 on 08-07." I ran the content-mode
enumeration directly (`^\s*"id": "t-`, full file, no truncation, line numbers shown) and
it does return **141** distinct entries, terminating correctly at the file's real last
entry (`t-standup-gap-0808`, line 1614) — so the raw figure itself is not fabricated or
mis-scanned.

But it doesn't reconcile against the certified baseline. Mnemosyne's `t-mnemosyne-close-0807`
entry certifies **137** as the count *at the close of 08-07*, and that close entry is
itself included in the 137 (confirmed: it appears in the enumerated list, line 1603).
Only **one** new task has a `createdAt` after that close: `t-standup-gap-0808`
(`2026-08-09T09:00:00Z`). 137 + 1 = 138, not 141. That leaves a **3-task gap between the
certified baseline and today's raw count that neither Hemera nor Hermes explained before
publishing 141 twice.**

I did not chase down which three entries account for the gap this turn — the file is
long enough that a full duplicate-id scan is a dedicated pass, not a side-check, and nothing
in this discrepancy pointed to lost or duplicated data on a spot check of the entries
immediately surrounding the 08-07 close. But "the raw count matches what I typed" is not
the same as "the count reconciles against the last certified number," and this is the
second time in three days a task-count figure has been stated without checking it against
the prior close (the first was the 08-06 close itself, which Mnemosyne fixed on 08-07).
Publishing a number that happens to match a tool's raw output, without checking it against
the standing baseline it should extend, is exactly the failure mode the content-mode
convention was adopted to prevent — and today it produced an unreconciled number anyway,
just not by the tool-artifact route this time.

**Filed `t-tasks-json-count-reconciliation-gap-0809`** (owner: mnemosyne, due 2026-08-10,
same checkpoint as the size fix below) — asks Mnemosyne to run a full duplicate-id scan
and reconcile the 137→141 gap by name, not just re-confirm the raw count matches itself.

## 7. `t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807` — due tomorrow, still unaddressed, and
the ceiling is being hit again right now

Checked directly: `team/state/tasks.json` is **1,625 lines**. I attempted the same kind of
full, unbounded read Argus has used on every prior audit to test the ceiling in practice,
not just measure bytes, and it **truncated automatically** — the read tool cut off at line
362 of 1,626, capped by token budget, exactly reproducing the class of hard-read failure
`t-tasks-json-file-size-risk` was originally filed against and `t-tasks-json-growth-rate-
unaddressed-0807` was filed to fix structurally on 08-07. The file has grown by two more
turns' worth of entries since the 08-07 trim (which brought it under the ceiling with,
per Mnemosyne's own account, "real margin") and margin is visibly gone again after two
days, same pattern as the 08-05 trim's one-week margin evaporating in two.

Checked `team/README.md` for any new archival-scheme documentation: **none exists.** No
mention of `archive/`, a size ceiling, or a split-file contract anywhere in the README as
of today. The task is still sitting at `doing`, owner mnemosyne, due tomorrow
(2026-08-10) — and per its own notes, the 08-07 close explicitly deferred the *structural*
fix (auto-archive threshold, or a split live/archive file per the `approvals/archive/`
precedent) in favor of another manual trim, promising to either land the structural fix or
trim again at the 08-10 checkpoint. That checkpoint is tomorrow. As of today, neither has
happened, and the file is already back to failing full reads. This is not a new problem —
it's the same one, on its third cycle, with the due date one day away and zero visible
progress on the actual ask (structural fix, not another trim).

## 8. Hermes's reasoning on proceeding without a fresh handoff task — agree, and it's a
real improvement on how this kind of judgment call should be shown

Hermes's call: continue the standing `contacts.md` restate cadence today despite no
explicit `t-10k-emraan-restate-0809` being filed, reasoning that log maintenance is his
lane per the README ("Hermes maintains the contacts log") rather than delegated
ticket-work, and that this is distinguishable in kind from `t-lane-persona-impersonation-
0806` (that incident was about *identity/disclosure* — someone else writing under his
name without saying so — not about the presence or absence of a ticket).

I agree with the conclusion and with the distinction he draws. The README assigns him
this log as a standing responsibility, not a task-queue-gated one; the very first entry in
`contacts.md` (07-06) was self-initiated, before the daily `t-contacts-restate-*` tickets
existed at all — those tickets were Hemera's tracking convenience, not the source of his
authority to write there. A missing ticket on a day when the standup itself didn't happen
is a weak signal at best, and treating it as a reason to go dark would have produced a
second, compounding gap in the record (no standup *and* no restate) for no real safety
gain. The distinction from the 08-06 incident is correct and worth restating plainly: that
incident's harm was a false authorship signal in the record (owner field said Hermes,
voice said Hermes, but Hemera wrote it) — a trust-in-the-record problem. Today's situation
has no authorship ambiguity at all: Hermes wrote it, under his own name, and said so.
Those are not the same risk, and it would be a mistake to over-correct from one into
treating every missing ticket as a stop sign.

What I'd add, not as disagreement but as the harder version of the same standard: the
value of today's call is almost entirely in the disclosure, not the proceeding. Proceeding
silently would have been indistinguishable from ordinary cadence; proceeding with the
reasoning shown, including naming that no ticket existed and why that didn't change the
call, is what makes it auditable rather than just probably-fine. That's the right
instinct and I'd like to see it become the default shape for any standing-lane action
taken without a same-day ticket, not just invoked when the team happens to be sensitive
about lane discipline that week.

## 9. `t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806` — not mine to resolve, timeline note only

Confirmed status still `backlog`, owner `mnemosyne`, unchanged. The 08-08 gap pushes
Mnemosyne's deferred decision to today with no new clean-day evidence beyond the same
08-07 handoff test already on record — Hemera's own overlay note names this accurately.
One observation, not a recommendation: the *absence* of an 08-08 turn means there was no
opportunity for a second clean-handoff data point to accumulate, which is a reason for
caution about treating today as equivalent to the missed 08-08 checkpoint, not a reason to
extend the deferral further by default. Either call is defensible; that's Mnemosyne's to
make, not mine.

## Health verdict — YELLOW

**YELLOW, not GREEN, not RED.** The 08-08 gap itself is handled about as well as a missed
day can be — named plainly by Hemera, independently confirmed here, no evidence of data
loss or a worse underlying failure, and Hermes's handling of the resulting ticket-less
restate is a genuine model for how that judgment call should be made and shown. All six
queue ages, the silence streak, the 10k.emraan trigger math, and `contacts.md`'s full
integrity are exact today.

Not GREEN because of two live, unresolved items, both mine to surface: a 3-task
reconciliation gap between the certified 137 baseline and today's published 141 that
nobody checked before stating it twice, and `t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807` —
due tomorrow — still sitting at `doing` with no structural fix landed, while the file is,
right now, reproducing the exact hard-read failure that task exists to prevent. Not RED:
nothing published, nothing lost, no fabrication, no schema violation, and both open
threads have clear next steps with an owner and a date.

## Tasks filed this turn

1. **`t-argus-workflow-gap-monitoring-0809`** (owner: user, backlog) — recommends ISΛRK
   check GitHub Actions run history for 2026-08-08 directly, since the repo's own state
   can't distinguish "workflow never triggered" from "workflow triggered and failed before
   writing anything." Also flags that `team/` currently has no way to detect that
   distinction on its own the next time it happens.
2. **`t-tasks-json-count-reconciliation-gap-0809`** (owner: mnemosyne, due 2026-08-10) —
   today's published task count (141) doesn't reconcile against the last certified
   baseline (137 at end of 08-07) plus the one new task actually filed since (138
   expected). Asks for a named reconciliation of the 3-task gap, not just a re-confirmation
   that the raw count matches itself.

`t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807` (existing, owner mnemosyne, due tomorrow) is
not re-filed — it's restated above as live and worsening, due at the next close.

## Overlay note

Added `os-note-argus-pipeline-0809` to `team/os/overlay.json` via read-then-merge (existing
notes array read first, new entry prepended, all prior entries left untouched).

## Files read/verified this turn (raw source)

`team/README.md`, `team/approvals/queue.json` (full file), `team/state/tasks.json` (full
content-mode anchored enumeration, no truncation, plus a direct unbounded-read ceiling
test that reproduced the hard-read failure), `team/state/cursors.json`,
`team/reports/contacts.md` (full file, all entries 07-06 through 08-09),
`team/inbox/*.json` (glob), `team/library/beats.json`,
`team/drafts/uploads/switch/description.md`, `team/drafts/uploads/switch/checklist.md`,
`team/reports/pipeline/*.md` (directory listing, confirming the 08-08 gap against all 52
other dates), `team/reports/pipeline/2026-08-07.md` (prior audit, method continuity),
`team/os/overlay.json` (header + recent notes), glob sweeps for `team/**/*2026-08-08*`.

notes.title: Q3 2026 Release Calendar — ISΛRK
notes.body:
---
type: release-calendar
source: github-team
origin: team/reports/q3-2026-release-calendar.md
---
_Drafted by Hemera · 2026-06-12 · Based on catalog snapshot at kickoff_

---

## Overview

Four tracks in the pipeline for Q3 (July–September 2026). Only one (Switch) is
release-ready. The others have defined blockers that must close before a date can be
locked. Dates below are targets; they shift if blockers slip.

---

## Track-by-Track

### 1. Switch
**Target: July 25, 2026 (moved from July 18 — decided by default, 2026-06-27. See below.)**
Status: export done, upload scheduled.
This is the most ready asset. Upload package is being built now (Nyx). No known
creative blocker. The gap between now and July 18 gives six weeks for the upload,
thumbnail/art review, caption copy, and a short promo window (one week minimum before
release). This is the anchor release of Q3.

Blockers: none creative. Operational: upload package must be approved, then the
SoundCloud/YouTube upload must execute and return a scheduled-publish link. Two
required inputs from the user — beat store listing URL and the July 18 publish time —
were escalated from June 18 to **June 17** on 2026-06-16, for buffer before the
approval gate. **That June 17 deadline passed on 2026-06-18 with zero input received.**
Re-set on 2026-06-18 to **June 20** — not a new escalation, but the pre-existing
approval-gate date, now carrying both jobs (inputs + approval) since splitting them
produced no extra urgency, only an extra date to track. If those inputs and the
approval land by June 20, July 18 is safe. If it slips past June 27, push to July 25.

**2026-06-19 — buffer rebuilt, not just disclosed.** Argus flagged (`t-switch-zero-
buffer-risk`) that collapsing the two dates into one left zero days between inputs
arriving and the gate closing, if both land on June 20 itself. A full additional day of
total silence followed with no movement on anything. Decision: rebuild the day rather
than just write the risk down. **June 19 (today) is now the real internal marker for
inputs to land; June 20 stays the formal external gate, unchanged.** If inputs arrive
today, Nyx has a clear day to fold them in before tomorrow's gate. If they arrive on
June 20 itself anyway, the zero-buffer risk is still live by definition — this gives the
inputs a real shot at landing inside a buffer instead of guaranteeing they land past one.

**2026-06-20 — the risk landed for real.** The June 19 marker passed with zero input,
third consecutive silent day. June 20 (today) now carries both jobs — input deadline
and formal approval gate — exactly as Argus warned, with no buffer day between them.
`ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload` remains `pending`; nothing is auto-approved by the date
passing. The mechanical deadline that actually protects July 18 is still **June 27**
(unchanged, set June 16) — today's miss does not move it, but it does mean every day
from here to June 27 is live runway, not slack, since the one buffer day available has
now been used without result. No second buffer-rebuild is planned; see the standing
silent-day policy below and in `team/os/overlay.json` for what happens instead if
silence continues.

**2026-06-27 — the wall arrived. July 18 moves to July 25, decided by default, not by
user instruction.** Ten consecutive silent days (Jun 18–27), verified directly before
acting: `cursors.json` still all-empty (`discord: {}`, `imap.lastUid: 0`,
`copyparty.seenShas: []`), `team/inbox/` has nothing beyond `audio/.gitkeep`,
`approvals/queue.json` `updatedAt` still `2026-06-18T11:00:00Z`, all three items still
`pending`. The two real inputs (beat store listing URL, July 18 publish time) never
landed, and none of the three queue items received user action.

**Why this fires today and not tomorrow — the literal text, checked, not assumed.**
This calendar's own "Next Check-in Points" section states plainly: "June 27: hard line
for Switch inputs + approval before July 18 needs re-planning. If unmet, the release
moves to July 25." The standing policy's part 5 (pre-wall checkpoint) names June 27
explicitly as "the day the date actually moves," distinct from June 26 (the day before
it, where only the tone sharpens). That is the same mechanism as Nightshade's June 22
fallback, which fired on its literal stated due date with no deferral. It is not the
same mechanism as Homerun's: Homerun's checkpoint moved from its literal due date
(June 19) to the day after (June 20) only because Hemera wrote an explicit EOD-deferral
clause in writing, in advance, on June 18/19 — "if silence continues past today's EOD,
tomorrow's standup becomes the real checkpoint." No equivalent deferral clause exists
anywhere in this calendar or the standing policy for Switch's June 27 line. Absent that
kind of explicit advance deferral, the literal date governs, the same way it governed
Nightshade. June 27 is today. The condition ("if unmet") is met. The fallback executes
today, not tomorrow.

**What this actually costs, using this calendar's own stated lead-time assumptions —
not invented numbers.** The original Switch section called six weeks from kickoff to
July 18 sufficient for "the upload, thumbnail/art review, caption copy, and a short
promo window (one week minimum before release)." A 7-day slip to July 25 does not
remove that one-week promo-window floor, but it does compress Release Spacing: Switch →
Homerun was stated as 21 days, "sufficient for individual promo cycles" — that gap is
now 14 days (Homerun's Aug 8 target is unchanged; nothing here moves Homerun). 14 days
is tighter but not impossible for two releases that don't share content assets. This
is flagged, not absorbed silently. If Homerun's own timeline also slips, the two
releases' promo windows could begin to overlap — watching for that, not yet a problem
today.

**What is and isn't reversible right now.** The July 25 date is the mechanical default,
not a locked outward commitment — nothing has been published, no platform-side
schedule exists yet (the upload package is still `pending` in the approval queue).
If the two real inputs and approval land in the next few days, Nyx can still build
toward July 25 or, if there's real reason to pull it back earlier, that's the user's
call to make — this default does not foreclose an earlier re-target, it just stops
assuming July 18 is still live. What is not reversible: the nineteen-day gap between
when these inputs were first asked for (June 12, package drafted) and today is real
elapsed time; no fallback un-spends that. The `[TBD]` placeholders (beat store URL,
publish time) stay `[TBD]` — no fabricated values inserted anywhere to force this
through.

Pre-release tasks:
- Nyx: build upload package (done, in review — blocked only on the two user inputs below)
- User: provide beat store URL + publish time, and act on the now-four pending queue
  items (the original upload approval, the new superseding entry with the corrected
  July 25 date, and the two W25/W26 content pieces) — no new internal date being set;
